page: Amazon Web Services r6i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The instance supplies 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache. It includes instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3.0 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Networking throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the average category across general compute, memory, and specialized testing suites. The CPU scores 1634.0 on Geekbench single-core, 9766.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and reaches a PassMark CPU score of 21093.88. In synthetic memory bandwidth tests, it records 828.29 GB/sec in small cached block reads (16 KB), 96.3 GB/sec in large-block reads (256 MB), and 57.12 GB/sec in large-block writes. Key workload metrics reflect strong data-handling capabilities, such as 15.38 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 21.16 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM density makes the r6i.4xlarge an efficient allocation of compute spending for systems that require extensive memory footprints without demanding proportional scaling of CPU cores. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators, limiting raw localized I/O speeds and intensive GPU compute pipelines. It is best suited for in-memory caching layers, relational and non-relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and general enterprise memory-heavy applications.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8375C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.5 GHz. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes a 54 MB L3 cache, AVX-512 vector support, and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across synthetic CPU and memory metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 9766.0, large-block memory read speeds of 96.3 GB/sec, and Redis throughput reaching 15.38 million SET operations per second. The server provides balanced resource density for memory-bound applications without forcing over-provisioning of CPU cores, making it well fitted for in-memory databases, caching tiers, analytics backends, and memory-intensive enterprise software.
